source: RFC 0014 R5 (mixed-version compatibility; maintainer's decisions of 2026-11-24 through the coordinator)
statement: Every CoSec process that reads the shared store through `cosec-cocache` writes its own status, whatever its pipeline mode and whether it shadows (a data-plane instance, a gateway, a control-plane host, an IAM service behind a gateway), with the CoSec release it runs, from the resource the build writes (`META-INF/cosec/release`, kept in a repackaged jar). It writes the first status as it starts, before its snapshot source reads a document, then every 10 seconds; with shadowing on, the shadow reporter writes it once a cycle after its reports, under the one instance id the reports use, and without, `shadows: false` and no windows, so no shadow window waits for it. A status key lives exactly an hour after its last write: the readers of the store are the statuses of the last hour (`GET /instances`), while an instance is live, for a window and `propagation`, only with a status from the last minute; the writers fix the hour, the upper bound of any reader set a later release may choose. A status without `release`, of a release before it, reads as an unknown release, which nothing in 8.0 counts or waits on. A status write that fails never stops the instance nor its start: it is logged once at ERROR, naming the keys its Redis user must be allowed to write, then at most once a minute, counted (`cosec.instance.status.failed`) and shown on the `cosecInstanceStatus` health indicator, which stays UP. A process without `cosec-cocache` writes none: the control plane cannot see it as a reader, and counts it nowhere (RFC 0014 §4).
